clauses.normalized_text: QUIC is a new multiplexed and secure transport atop UDP.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC is a new multiplexed and secure transport atop UDP.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC builds on decades of transport and security experience, and implements mechanisms that make it attractive as a modern general-purpose transport.

clauses.normalized_text: All transmissions in QUIC are sent with a packet-level header, which includes a packet sequence number (referred to below as a packet number).
clauses.raw_text: All transmissions in QUIC are sent with a packet-level header, which includes a packet sequence number (referred to below as a packet number).
clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: These packet numbers never repeat in the lifetime of a connection, and are monotonically increasing, which makes duplicate detection trivial.
clauses.raw_text: These packet numbers never repeat in the lifetime of a connection, and are monotonically increasing, which makes duplicate detection trivial.

clauses.normalized_text: This fundamental design decision obviates the need for disambiguating between transmissions and retransmissions and eliminates significant complexity from QUIC’s interpretation of TCP loss detection mechanisms.
clauses.raw_text: This fundamental design decision obviates the need for disambiguating between transmissions and retransmissions and eliminates significant complexity from QUIC’s interpretation of TCP loss detection mechanisms.

clauses.section_heading: Design of the QUIC Transmission Machinery

clauses.normalized_text: There are some notable differences between QUIC and TCP which are important for reasoning about the differences between the loss recovery mechanisms employed by the two protocols.
clauses.raw_text: There are some notable differences between QUIC and TCP which are important for reasoning about the differences between the loss recovery mechanisms employed by the two protocols.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: We briefly describe these differences below.
clauses.raw_text: We briefly describe these differences below.
clauses.section_heading: Relevant Differences Between QUIC and TCP

clauses.normalized_text: TCP conflates transmission sequence number at the sender with delivery sequence number at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently to problems caused by “retransmission ambiguity”.
clauses.raw_text: TCP conflates transmission sequence number at the sender with delivery sequence number at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently to problems caused by “retransmission ambiguity”.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet sequence number (referred to as the “packet number”) for transmissions, and any data that is to be delivered to the receiving application(s) is sent in one or more streams, with stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames inside of packets that determine delivery order.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet sequence number (referred to as the “packet number”) for transmissions, and any data that is to be delivered to the receiving application(s) is sent in one or more streams, with stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames inside of packets that determine delivery order.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing, and directly encodes transmission order.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing, and directly encodes transmission order.

clauses.normalized_text: A higher QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.
clauses.raw_text: A higher QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower QUIC packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.

clauses.normalized_text: When a packet containing frames is deemed lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.
clauses.raw_text: When a packet containing frames is deemed lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.

clauses.normalized_text: Consequently, more accurate RTT measurements can be made, spurious retransmissions are trivially detected, and mechanisms such as Fast Retransmit can be applied universally, based only on packet number.
clauses.raw_text: Consequently, more accurate RTT measurements can be made, spurious retransmissions are trivially detected, and mechanisms such as Fast Retransmit can be applied universally, based only on packet number.

clauses.normalized_text: This design point significantly simplifies loss detection mechanisms for QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: This design point significantly simplifies loss detection mechanisms for QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: Most TCP mechanisms implicitly attempt to infer transmission ordering based on TCP sequence numbers - a non-trivial task, especially when TCP timestamps are not available.
clauses.raw_text: Most TCP mechanisms implicitly attempt to infer transmission ordering based on TCP sequence numbers - a non-trivial task, especially when TCP timestamps are not available.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is equivalent to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is equivalent to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC supports up to 256 ACK ranges, opposed to TCP’s 3 SACK ranges.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC supports up to 256 ACK ranges, opposed to TCP’s 3 SACK ranges.

clauses.normalized_text: In high loss environments, this speeds recovery.
clauses.raw_text: In high loss environments, this speeds recovery.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ACKs explicitly encode the delay incurred at the receiver between when a packet is received and when the corresponding ACK is sent.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs explicitly encode the delay incurred at the receiver between when a packet is received and when the corresponding ACK is sent.

clauses.normalized_text: This allows the receiver of the ACK to adjust for receiver delays, specifically the delayed ack timer, when estimating the path RTT.
clauses.raw_text: This allows the receiver of the ACK to adjust for receiver delays, specifically the delayed ack timer, when estimating the path RTT.

clauses.normalized_text: This mechanism also allows a receiver to measure and report the delay from when a packet was received by the OS kernel, which is useful in receivers which may incur delays such as context-switch latency before a userspace QUIC receiver processes a received packet.
clauses.raw_text: This mechanism also allows a receiver to measure and report the delay from when a packet was received by the OS kernel, which is useful in receivers which may incur delays such as context-switch latency before a userspace QUIC receiver processes a received packet.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements the spirit of a variety of RFCs, Internet drafts, and other well-known TCP loss recovery mechanisms, though the implementation details differ from the TCP implementations.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements the spirit of a variety of RFCs, Internet drafts, and other well-known TCP loss recovery mechanisms, though the implementation details differ from the TCP implementations.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC calculates SRTT and RTTVAR according to the standard formulas.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC calculates SRTT and RTTVAR according to the standard formulas.

clauses.normalized_text: An RTT sample is only taken if the delayed ack correction is smaller than the measured RTT (otherwise a negative RTT would result), and the ack’s contains a new, larger largest observed packet number. min_rtt is only based on the observed RTT, but SRTT uses the delayed ack correction delta.
clauses.raw_text: An RTT sample is only taken if the delayed ack correction is smaller than the measured RTT (otherwise a negative RTT would result), and the ack’s contains a new, larger largest observed packet number. min_rtt is only based on the observed RTT, but SRTT uses the delayed ack correction delta.

clauses.normalized_text: As described above, QUIC implements RTO with the standard timeout and CWND reduction.
clauses.raw_text: As described above, QUIC implements RTO with the standard timeout and CWND reduction.

clauses.normalized_text: However, QUIC retransmits the earliest outstanding packets rather than the latest, because QUIC doesn’t have retransmission ambiguity.
clauses.raw_text: However, QUIC retransmits the earliest outstanding packets rather than the latest, because QUIC doesn’t have retransmission ambiguity.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC uses the commonly accepted min RTO of 200ms instead of the 1s the RFC specifies.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC uses the commonly accepted min RTO of 200ms instead of the 1s the RFC specifies.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements the algorithm for early loss recovery described in the FACK paper (and implemented in the Linux kernel.)
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements the algorithm for early loss recovery described in the FACK paper (and implemented in the Linux kernel.)

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC uses the packet number to measure the FACK reordering threshold.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC uses the packet number to measure the FACK reordering threshold.

clauses.normalized_text: Currently QUIC does not implement an adaptive threshold as many TCP implementations (i.e., the Linux kernel) do.
clauses.raw_text: Currently QUIC does not implement an adaptive threshold as many TCP implementations (i.e., the Linux kernel) do.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC only reduces its CWND once per congestion window, in keeping with the NewReno RFC.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC only reduces its CWND once per congestion window, in keeping with the NewReno RFC.

clauses.normalized_text: It tracks the largest outstanding packet at the time the loss is declared and any losses which occur before that packet number are considered part of the same loss event.
clauses.raw_text: It tracks the largest outstanding packet at the time the loss is declared and any losses which occur before that packet number are considered part of the same loss event.

clauses.normalized_text: It’s worth noting that some TCP implementations may do this on a sequence number basis, and hence consider multiple losses of the same packet a single loss event.
clauses.raw_text: It’s worth noting that some TCP implementations may do this on a sequence number basis, and hence consider multiple losses of the same packet a single loss event.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC always sends two tail loss probes before RTO is triggered.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC always sends two tail loss probes before RTO is triggered.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC invokes tail loss probe even when a loss is outstanding, which is different than some TCP implementations.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC invokes tail loss probe even when a loss is outstanding, which is different than some TCP implementations.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements early retransmit with a timer in order to minimize spurious retransmits.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements early retransmit with a timer in order to minimize spurious retransmits.

clauses.normalized_text: The timer is set to 1/4 SRTT after the final outstanding packet is acked.
clauses.raw_text: The timer is set to 1/4 SRTT after the final outstanding packet is acked.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements F-RTO by not reducing the CWND and SSThresh until a subsequent ack is received and it’s sure the RTO was not spurious.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements F-RTO by not reducing the CWND and SSThresh until a subsequent ack is received and it’s sure the RTO was not spurious.

clauses.normalized_text: Conceptually this is similar, but it makes for a much cleaner implementation with fewer edge cases.
clauses.raw_text: Conceptually this is similar, but it makes for a much cleaner implementation with fewer edge cases.

clauses.normalized_text: PRR-SSRB is implemented by QUIC in the epoch when recovering from a loss.
clauses.raw_text: PRR-SSRB is implemented by QUIC in the epoch when recovering from a loss.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP Cubic is the default congestion control algorithm in QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: TCP Cubic is the default congestion control algorithm in QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: Reno is also an easily available option which may be requested via connection options and is fully implemented.
clauses.raw_text: Reno is also an easily available option which may be requested via connection options and is fully implemented.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements hybrid slow start, but disables ack train detection, because it has shown to falsely trigger when coupled with packet pacing, which is also on by default in QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements hybrid slow start, but disables ack train detection, because it has shown to falsely trigger when coupled with packet pacing, which is also on by default in QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: Currently the minimum delay increase is 4ms, the maximum is 16ms, and within that range QUIC exits slow start if the min_rtt within a round increases by more than one eighth of the connection mi

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s loss detection is by it’s time-ordered nature, very similar to RACK.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s loss detection is by it’s time-ordered nature, very similar to RACK.
